findings.title: Write lock is held across CDN and file I/O, blocking all readers
findings.body: The write lock is acquired at line 48 and held via defer for the whole rebuild, including `readWebAssetsFromCDN`, which performs an HTTP request bounded only by the caller's context. While a cache miss or dev-mode reload is in progress, every concurrent `GetWebAssets` call blocks on `RLock` at line 41, even though a valid cached value may exist. Before this change, readers never blocked. A slow or hung CDN can therefore stall all page renders that go through this function.

findings.title: No double-check after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: After the RLock check at lines 41-47 fails, the goroutine takes the write lock without re-reading `entryPointAssetsCache`. Every goroutine that observed a nil cache at the same time will repeat the full manifest load and CDN fetch, and each will overwrite the global in turn. The lock prevents a data race, but it does not prevent this duplicated work or the last-writer-wins churn on a cold start.

findings.title: No test covers the concurrent access this change is meant to fix
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the package-level cache, but it adds no test that exercises `GetWebAssets` from multiple goroutines. Without a `-race` test, nothing guards against regressions. A test that runs concurrent calls in both dev and non-dev modes would verify the fix.
